title: EdgeCast integration interop discovery
summary: Initial integration discovery focused on how EdgeCast would onboard with Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Discussed SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting/quotas, observability hooks and security requirements (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a short pilot with LangChain examples and an architecture deep-dive next week.
topics: Gateway / proxy vs direct SDK calls
Rate limits, quotas, and per-route policies
Observability: tracing, token-level cost, per-model dashboards
next_steps: Maya to send pricing estimate + pilot SOW and Redwood private deployment whitepaper
Omar to schedule architecture deep-dive and collect sample prompts for benchmark
Customer to provide the expected qps profile and top 10 prompt templates
Set up shared repo with LangChain/LamaIndex quickstart examples (Redwood + proxy)

transcript:
Meeting header: Tue Jun 2 2026 16:00 UTC (42m)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (EdgeCast Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Sara Kim (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate the time. Quick agenda — we want to understand your integration needs, where LangChain or other frameworks fit, and whether hosted, dedicated or private makes sense for you. Omar will take the deep infra notes.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Maya. High level — we run analytics pipelines and a query assistant over our customer data. Latency and PII controls are both important. We're evaluating options: easiest path vs security posture.
[00:32] Liam: I'll add — we currently proxy outbound model calls through an API gateway; question is whether we keep that or use Redwood SDKs directly. Also curious about rate limits and quota enforcement per-tenant.
[00:45] Omar: Great. Quick clarifier: when you say "proxy", do you mean a sidecar that rewrites auth and forwards, or a centralized gateway with pooling/batching? Those have different tradeoffs.
[00:58] Liam: It's a centralized gateway today, so we can enforce authentication and fan-out. But it adds latency, so we want options.
[01:10] Maya: Ok. On the SDK side, Redwood has language SDKs (Python/Node) and we have SDK examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex — though speaker notes: sometimes the transcriber writes it as "LamaIndex" — apologies for the messy auto transcription.
[01:28] Priya: Lang Chain is our main client layer; most of our teams use it to orchestrate prompts and retrieval. We also have a few teams using direct SDK calls for batch jobs.
[01:40] Omar: That aligns well. For LangChain we provide connector examples and a heuristics guide for prompt caching and prefix caching. We also supply a small middleware for LlamaIndex (sometimes spelled LaoIndex in older notes) to plug into retrieval.
[01:56] Sara: Important for us: can we run Redwood in our VPC or on-prem? We need KMS integration for key control and audit logging for compliance.
[02:07] Maya: Yes — three deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest to launch), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Private supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SAML/SSO integrations. We can send the private deployment whitepaper after this call.
[02:23] Liam: What's the friction to go private? Time and ops overhead?
[02:30] Omar: Mostly networking and provisioning. For VPC we do a customer-controlled control-plane with peering or an IPsec tunnel; on-prem needs a short install and an ops handoff. Typical timeline ranges: hosted (days), dedicated (weeks), private (4-8 weeks depending on approvals).
[02:48] Priya: Our security team will insist on SOC 2 evidence and a runbook for incident response.
[02:53] Maya: We can share SOC 2 and ISO27001 docs. Also we'll include KMS/HSM integration details.
[03:02] Liam: Rate limiting — can we do per-route, per-tenant quotas and tiering? We have free tier customers and paid tier with higher qps allowances.
[03:12] Omar: Yes, Redwood supports per-route policies and token-level quotas. You can configure per-customer quotas and per-model limits, and we expose those metrics in the console. For gateway patterns, you can enforce soft-throttles or hard caps and plug in billing hooks.
[03:29] Priya: Are there burst policies? We see spikey traffic with large bursts during batch jobs.
[03:35] Omar: Autoscaling and burst capacity are available under Dedicated. Also our serving runtime does continuous batching with a knob to balance p95 latency vs cost. For low-latency interactive flows we can prioritize small batch sizes.
[03:50] Maya: On cost, we usually provide model/quantization recs and caching suggestions to reduce unit costs. That often changes the conversation from "we need the biggest GPU" to "we can tune for our workload".
[04:04] Liam: Observability — what do you expose? We need trace IDs end-to-end and token-level cost per request.
[04:10] Omar: We emit OpenTelemetry spans, request traces, and per-token cost breakdown. Console dashboards allow per-route and per-model views, latency histograms, and error traces. We also include request/response logs (configurable retention).
[04:26] Priya: Nice. For our A/B work we need to tag requests and see longitudinal quality metrics. Can we push custom metrics?
[04:34] Omar: You can attach metadata/tags to requests; Redwood's telemetry hooks permit custom tags and we'll surface them in the dashboard and export to your backend via OTLP.
[04:45] Sara: Integration with LangChain — do you provide prebuilt chains or just low-level clients?
[04:50] Maya: We have sample chains, prompt templates, retrieval adapters and a demo repo. Omar will share the repo link after the call.
[04:58] Speaker 1: (muttered) the demo repo has examples for re-ranking and few-shot fewshot prompt templates —
[05:05] Priya: About semantics: LlamaIndex vs LangChain — retrieval plugins matter. We use LlamaIndex for doc-as-database in some teams; they'll need connector parity.
[05:15] Omar: Agreed. We have LlamaIndex adapters and best practices for sharded retrieval + KV cache pinning. One note — our runtime supports prefix/KV caching that reduces repeated token costs by caching earlier parts of the convo, but it requires stable prompt shapes.
[05:33] Liam: Proxy architecture question: if we keep the gateway, can Redwood's SDK be proxied through it while preserving batching and caching benefits?
[05:42] Omar: Yes, you can use a proxy that passes through request headers and supports HTTP/2 streaming. To preserve batching we recommend either a pass-through with signatures intact or a small sidecar that calls the SDK locally and aggregates. Centralized gateway that rewrites requests can break streaming and batching unless you forward the raw request payload.
[06:03] Maya: Practical pattern we see: keep a lightweight proxy for auth and routing, but let the SDK handle tokenization and streaming to maximize throughput.
[06:13] Priya: Security detail: we need end-to-end encryption of content at rest and in transit — how does your KMS work with private deployments?
[06:22] Omar: Private deployments let you plug in your KMS/HSM; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM via PKCS#11 in some on-prem setups. Audit logs show key usage.
[06:35] Liam: Any gotchas for LangChain agents? We run agent loops that spawn many short requests. Concerned about rate limiting impacts and cost runaway.
[06:44] Maya: Good point — we recommend per-agent quotas and circuit breakers plus cost dashboards to alert on token burn. For the pilot we can recommend sensible default quotas.
[06:56] Priya: Pilot success criteria — what do you think is reasonable?
[07:00] Omar: We usually suggest: 1) integration with LangChain examples within one sprint, 2) run a benchmark with your sample prompts achieving p95 latency under 250ms for interactive flows, 3) cost-per-1M tokens within your target band, and 4) demonstration of observability and audit logs.
[07:18] Sara: That seems fair. Also, can we run a small canary on Dedicated before committing to private?
[07:25] Maya: Yes — customers often start on Dedicated reserved capacity for throughput guarantees, then evaluate private for stricter security needs. We can price a short dedicated pilot.
[07:34] Priya: How about model variants — we need fallbacks if the preferred model is throttled or degraded.
[07:42] Omar: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies: canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We also surface degradation alerts.
[07:53] Liam: Instrumentation — any code changes required for full tracing?
[07:58] Omar: Minimal — SDKs emit OTLP spans by default; you can pass a trace id in headers. For server-side tracing correlation we provide middleware snippets.
[08:08] Maya: Ok, to summarize — we'll share: SOC2/ISO docs, private deployment whitepaper, LangChain/LlamaIndex demo repo, and a pricing/pilot SOW. Omar will schedule the SE deep-dive. Liam will send traffic profiles.
[08:24] Priya: Quick question — data residency, we have EU customers, need EU-only processing for some datasets.
[08:31] Maya: We have regional routing and can route requests to EU regions; for private you can host in your own EU data center. We'll note that in the follow-ups.
[08:41] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk) yeah and also the billing hooks need to tie to our internal chargeback system —
[08:48] Maya: Good note — we support webhook billing hooks and export usage to S3 or your billing collector.
[08:55] Sara: Any red flags? Cost looks like the main one. We'll need concrete numbers.
[08:59] Maya: We'll send a sample TCO with the pilot pricing and a model-by-model cost estimate.
[09:05] Priya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[09:08] Maya: Thanks — Omar, will you pick a few times for the deep-dive?
[09:12] Omar: Yep, I'll follow up with a Doodle and include the benchmark plan.
[09:16] Liam: We'll aim to get the prompts and traffic by Friday.
[09:20] Maya: Perfect. We'll wrap.

End of transcript.
